coordinate_space: Position space, X right / Y down, origin at the feet/action anchor; per-frame pivot_px is that anchor inside the cell (uv top-left relative, y down)

transform_semantics.rotation_direction: positive degrees rotate counterclockwise in y-down image space (PIL rotate(+angle), anchor at image center)
transform_semantics.rotation_anchor_basis: ground-contact fit: minimize max |bottom_y| (lowest visible body pixel vs y=0 in position space) over all 10 rotated swordman frames (overturn/recovery rolls/dodge), body mask, CCW convention; method calibrated on the fighter where the same fit recovers the M6-020 verified anchor (250,292) within 10 px (fit (248,301) err 12.0 vs shipped (250,292) err 20.3, overturn span at fit anchor -78..+12 matches the M6-020 overturn damage box 0..78). Not native-code verified; same epistemic status as the M6-020 fighter anchor.

weapon_rule.note: katana0000b/c are the behind/front split of one sword (verify draw_order katana0000b->body->...->katana0000c).  The M8-016 card asked to take b OR c per pose per the verify "mutually exclusive per pose" wording, but frame-level verification (layer_data_probe.json: 100/179 indices non-empty on BOTH layers, e.g. rest f0 b=57px scabbard + c=799px sword; agrees with M8-003 spotcheck stats) disproved exclusivity, so both composite in the verified z-order.
